solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Argument raised temper, bringing in women's bitter stuff

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word for argument is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a row is a quarrel

indicators.note: the mood takes in the women's letter, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a temper is a mood
W is the standard abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A quarrel flares up and someone's temper absorbs women's bitter remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' reads the argument word upwards; 'bringing in' sets the women's letter just after the first letter of the temper word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wormwood is a plant famous for its bitterness, used in absinthe and as a byword for bitterness.

clue.text: Understanding offering to cut out noise

indicators.note: the clue tells us to remove the word for noise from the offering, a plain deletion signal

parts.note: handing something over is offering it
din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: Someone grasps the idea of offering earplugs to block out noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking DIN out of HANDING leaves the four letters; the definition works through the idiom 'get the hang of'.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the hang of something is to grasp it, so the noun names a knack or comprehension.

clue.text: More nervous broadcasting boss — that is, with Queen coming round

indicators.note: the queen's letters surround the rest, so this signals one piece placed around another

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen
DG is the Director-General, head of the BBC
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: A jittery BBC chief becomes even more anxious when the Queen visits.
explanation.walkthrough: The Director-General (DG) runs the BBC, Britain's public broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy is a colloquial synonym for nervous or tense, and this is its comparative form.

clue.text: Playboy's granted time inside for some gambling?

indicators.note: the granted and time pieces go inside the playboy word, a plain containment signal

parts.note: a roue is a dissolute pleasure-seeking man; the 's means has
to let is to allow or grant

explanation.surface: A rake allowed out of prison for a while hits the casino tables.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the game is an example of gambling, not a synonym for it.
explanation.definitionFit: This wheel-and-ball casino game is one particular form of betting, hence an example with a query.

clue.text: Item of furniture I found in crumbling rectories

indicators.note: the single letter I is located within the rearranged letters, a containment signal
crumbling buildings fall apart, so the letters of rectories are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture turns up among decaying vicarages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbling' rearranges RECTORIES into ESCRITORE, then 'found in' places the I between O and RE.
explanation.definitionFit: An escritoire is a writing desk, a classic piece of antique furniture.

clue.text: Put out? Daughter's put out, occupying chair

indicators.note: here put out means pushed outwards, so the daughter's letter is shifted to the very end

parts.note: to sedate a patient is to put them out, knock them unconscious with drugs
D is the abbreviation for daughter; the 's means is

explanation.surface: Is someone offended? The daughter has been ejected from her seat at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' appears twice with two jobs: first as the verb for drugging someone unconscious, then as the instruction to push the daughter's letter out to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sitting down is in a chair, so being sat describes occupying it.

clue.text: Firm with planetary explorer, one unable to collect water

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a lander is a spacecraft that touches down on a planet

explanation.surface: A company building a Mars probe that cannot collect water samples.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen strainer is perforated, so it lets liquid drain away rather than holding it.

clue.text: Stone blocking line, creating minor commotion

indicators.note: the stone sits within the line, blocking it, which signals containment

parts.note: a rule is a straight line
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: A rock obstructing the railway causes a small disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustle is a soft crackling stir, a small fuss of sound such as leaves make.

clue.text: Inspectorate frequently probed by Sun editor

indicators.note: the sun and editor pieces push into the frequently word, a containment signal

parts.note: oft is an old word for often
S is the abbreviation for Sun, as in Sunday

explanation.surface: A schools watchdog repeatedly investigated by the editor of a tabloid newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid, which makes 'Sun editor' look like one person.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the English body that inspects schools, an official inspection agency.

clue.text: Unduly confident detective returned, ignoring garden

indicators.note: returned signals the remaining letters are read back to front
ignoring means leaving out the garden word from the detective

parts.note: gumshoe is American slang for a private detective
to hoe is to work a garden

explanation.surface: A cocky detective came back and paid no attention to the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garden' is a verb here, as in working the soil; 'ignoring' takes that word out of the American slang for a private eye before 'returned' reverses what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Being self-satisfied means being complacently pleased with oneself, overly sure.

clue.text: Elected members' acclaim by public (dispensing champagne) is seen in isolation

parts.note: the ins are those in office, as opposed to the outs

indicators.note: dispensing with something means doing without, so the champagne word is removed

parts.note: popularity is general public approval
pop is informal for fizzy drink such as champagne

explanation.surface: MPs being cheered while the champagne flows, though cut off from everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ins' are the party in power. 'dispensing' removes POP, leaving ULARITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Insularity is the state of being cut off and inward-looking, like an island, hence isolation.

clue.text: Daughter with wet blanket not at first someone looking for water

indicators.note: the first letter of the wet blanket word is dropped

parts.note: wowser is Australian slang for a killjoy or puritan

explanation.surface: A daughter teams up with a killjoy who has a slow start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not at first' drops the W of WOWSER, an Australian word for a prudish spoilsport.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowser uses a forked rod to search for underground springs.

clue.text: Bacteria sprinkled on all meals

indicators.note: sprinkled scatters the letters of on, all and meals into a new order

explanation.surface: Germs dusted over every dish served.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten letters of ON ALL MEALS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a genus of rod-shaped microbes that cause food poisoning.

clue.text: Freedom's commonplace when power's deposed

indicators.note: deposed means ousted, so the power letter is removed

parts.note: a platitude is a trite remark, a commonplace
P is the abbreviation for power; the 's means is

explanation.surface: Talk of liberty becomes a cliche once the regime is overthrown.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude means scope or room to act as one chooses, a synonym for freedom.

clue.text: Cash sum accepted by staff to be returned

indicators.note: returned tells us the combined letters are read backwards
the sum is taken in by the staff, a containment signal

parts.note: a rod is a stick or staff
all is the total, the whole sum

explanation.surface: Money handed over to employees must be paid back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' is a stick, not employees. 'accepted by' gives RALLOD, which 'to be returned' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: The dollar is a currency unit, so it stands for money in general.

clue.text: A couple of lines on university's small bottle of watery deposits

parts.note: L is line, so two lines give LL
U is the abbreviation for university
a vial is a small glass container

explanation.surface: A scholar's poem of two lines written on a tiny flask.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective describes sediment laid down by flowing rivers and floods.

clue.text: Soldiers run, escaping from confinement

indicators.note: the run letter gets out of the confinement word, which signals removal

parts.note: a leg iron is a shackle that confines a prisoner
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Troops flee after breaking out of prison.
explanation.walkthrough: A leg iron is a shackle; 'escaping from' removes its R.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion is a large body of troops, originally a Roman army unit.

clue.text: Mostly unpleasant question about Ali's flowing script

indicators.note: about signals that the outer letters go round Ali
mostly means the last letter of the word for unpleasant is dropped

parts.note: nasty means unpleasant
Ali is a man's name; the 's is possessive

explanation.surface: A nasty query about the boxer's handwriting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims NASTY to NAST; NAST plus Q goes 'about' ALI.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Persian calligraphic hand with flowing, sloping strokes.

clue.text: Caught the Parisienne being embraced by German and naked

indicators.note: embraced means held within, so the caught and Parisienne pieces sit inside

parts.note: und is German for and
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
la is French feminine for the

explanation.surface: A Parisian woman caught in a German's arms, wearing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclad means without clothes, which is a plain synonym for nude.

clue.text: Tolerate US city line taking roundabout route for one of its boroughs

parts.note: to brook is to tolerate

indicators.note: roundabout here means turning back, so the city and line letters are reversed

parts.note: NY is New York

explanation.surface: Putting up with a New York subway line that wanders the long way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' refers back to the US city, New York, of which this is a borough.
explanation.definitionFit: Brooklyn is one of the five administrative divisions of New York City.

clue.text: Cutting device with a cut-down spike, face upwards

indicators.note: in a down clue, facing upwards means the letters are read from bottom to top
cut down means shortened, so the last letter of the spike word goes

parts.note: a spire is a tapering point, a spike

explanation.surface: A tool fitted with a shortened spike, lying face up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut-down' trims SPIRE to SPIR; 'face upwards' reverses WASPIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A ripsaw is a coarse saw for cutting timber along the grain.

clue.text: About to participate in gossip before English musical

indicators.note: before places the first part ahead of the English letter
the about word joins in, taking part inside the gossip word

parts.note: gas is idle chatter
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Getting involved in tittle-tattle ahead of a West End show.
explanation.definitionFit: Grease is the 1970s stage show and film about American high-school life, a well-known musical.

clue.text: Small stones start to rattle, pounded by hammer

indicators.note: the start letter is hit and enclosed by the hammer, a containment signal

parts.note: a gavel is a judge's or auctioneer's hammer

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of rattle

explanation.surface: Pebbles begin to clatter when struck by a mallet.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravel is loose small pebbles, as on a drive or path.

clue.text: Country once rigged popular vote, one over seceding

indicators.note: a rigged ballot is fixed, so the letters of popular vote are rearranged

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over, and one of the two O letters leaves

explanation.surface: A nation where the popular vote was fixed, with one region breaking away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seceding' says one O leaves the letters of POPULAR VOTE before they are rearranged. Upper Volta was renamed Burkina Faso in 1984.
explanation.definitionFit: This West African state existed under that name until 1984, hence a country of the past.

clue.text: Intend prisoner mostly to remain within confines of prison

indicators.note: the shortened prisoner stays inside the outer letters, a containment signal
confines are boundaries, so take the outer letters of prison
mostly means the last letter of the prisoner word is dropped

parts.note: lag is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: A convict means to stay behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confines of' gives P and N from prison; 'mostly' cuts LAG to LA.
explanation.definitionFit: To plan something is to mean or aim to do it.

clue.text: Lawyer's last to enter agreement about victim

indicators.note: the lawyer's final letter goes inside the reversed agreement, a containment signal
about means turned round, so the agreement word is read backwards

parts.note: yep is an informal yes

indicators.note: last means the final letter of lawyer

explanation.surface: A lawyer finally strikes a deal concerning the injured party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns YEP into PEY, then the R from 'Lawyer's last' enters it.
explanation.definitionFit: Prey is a creature hunted or a person exploited, hence a victim.

clue.text: Trouble experienced when turning over item in flowerbed

indicators.note: turning over signals the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
had means underwent, experienced

explanation.surface: Gardening woe: something goes wrong when digging over a bed of plants.
explanation.definitionFit: This showy tuberous bloom is commonly grown in garden borders, so it is an example.

clue.text: End tense, having recalled quote about regime

parts.note: to die is to end
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the quote word is read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: A tense ending to a speech after someone retracts a quotation about the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regime' is an eating regimen here, not a government.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective relates to diet, and a diet is a nutritional regimen.
